description: CRR3 contains the output floor at 72.5% of standardised approach RWA
CRR3 contains the revised standardised approach for credit risk
CRR3 contains the FRTB market risk framework
CRR3 contains the new standardised approach for operational risk
CRR3 contains the IRRBB Pillar 1 capital requirement for outliers
CRD6 contains the CSRBB supervisory requirement
CRD6 contains the harmonised third-country branch regime
CRD6 contains ESG risk integration requirements for banks
CRD6 contains enhanced fit and proper requirements
MiCA contains Art.3 defining all key MiCA terms
MiCA contains Art.16 on ART authorisation
MiCA contains Art.43 on EMT authorisation via credit institutions/EMIs
MiCA contains Art.59 on CASP authorisation
MiCA contains Art.76 prohibiting market abuse in crypto-assets
MiCA contains Art.83 cross-referencing AML/CFT requirements for CASPs
MiCA contains Art.147 on ESMA's supervisory powers
CRR3 implements and revises the Pillar 1 minimum capital requirement framework
CRD6 implements and updates the Pillar 2 ICAAP/SREP framework
CRR3 implements and expands Pillar 3 market discipline disclosures
Output floor constrains minimum RWA to 72.5% of standardised approach level, reducing internal model benefit
Revised SA credit risk is primary determinant of RWA for standardised banks
FRTB determines market risk component of RWA
New SMA determines operational risk component of RWA
IRRBB (Pillar 1 for outliers) and CSRBB (Pillar 2 supervisory requirement) are related interest/spread rate risk frameworks
Pillar 1 minimum requirements are complemented by Pillar 2 additional requirements set by supervisors in SREP
Pillar 2 capital add-ons and risk assessments are disclosed through Pillar 3 reports
ESG risk integration (CRD6) requires ESG risks to be covered in ICAAP and SREP assessments
MiCA Art.3 defines the CASP concept and its constituent services
MiCA Art.3 defines asset-referenced token (ART)
MiCA Art.3 defines e-money token (EMT)
CASPs are authorised under MiCA Art.59
ART issuers are authorised under MiCA Art.16
EMT issuers are authorised under MiCA Art.43
Significant tokens can be a subset of ARTs meeting threshold criteria
Significant tokens can be a subset of EMTs meeting threshold criteria
Significant ART/EMT issuers are subject to additional EBA supervision under MiCA
MiCA Art.83 AML/CFT obligations are detailed in the MiCA × AMLR cross-reference
TFR crypto Travel Rule implements the AML transfer transparency obligation referenced in MiCA Art.83
EBA develops RTS, ITS and guidelines implementing CRR3 requirements
EBA develops standards for CRD6 implementation including SREP guidelines
ESMA maintains the EU-wide CASP authorisation register
ESMA exercises its direct supervisory powers for crypto-assets under MiCA Art.147
ECB/SSM conducts SREP for significant institutions under its direct supervision
CRR/AMLR cross-reference documents AML fine and op-risk capital interactions
MiCA × AMLR cross-reference documents CASP AML/CFT obligations and Travel Rule
CRR × DORA cross-reference documents ICT risk and operational risk capital interaction
MiCA × GDPR cross-reference documents CASP personal data processing tensions
CRD6 ESG risk (including governance/financial crime dimension) is part of broader CRR/AMLR governance interaction
